title: The Costing
description: Because somebody asked where a cleared town goes, the meeting at Number Nine has sent an assessor up the valley to cost the removal of Rivermark: carts, roofs, wages, a year's bread, the burying ground. She counts what is under each head and puts down nothing else.

the_heads.title: Five heads
the_heads.objective: Hesper Amsel is costing Rivermark on Granary Row. Decide what she should count.
the_heads.journal: An assessor from Number Nine, Hesper Amsel, is on the granary steps costing the removal of Rivermark under five heads Hollin Sare wrote: carts, roofs, wages, a year's bread, the burying ground. She counts what is under each head, and nothing else.

counted_whole.title: Not otherwise provided for
counted_whole.journal: I walked Hesper Amsel round everything that wasn't under a head: Osric's remedies, the nine families Dagen Wyke has in pencil, the fen-root beds, Pol's weighing floor. She wrote a sixth head at the foot of Mr Sare's list in her own hand, Not otherwise provided for, and counted under it for two days. The figure is honest and it is large. It is still a figure. The meeting will read it next quarter, and I do not know what they will decide. Her count goes down to Minna Crale at Number Nine on the next packet, and whatever the house makes of it will be waiting there.

counted_given.title: Five heads, exactly
counted_given.journal: Hesper Amsel counted what was under the five heads, exactly, and nothing else. It took her nine days. The figure is honest about everything it counts. Her count goes down to Minna Crale at Number Nine on the next packet, and whatever the house makes of it will be waiting there.
